Compress Presentation, Never Truth — the Barkpark Context-Compression Program

content.value: Headroom is a 61,459-star proxy that guesses what to compress — and its own 3,900-line self-audit concludes the guessing was the bug. Barkpark does not need to guess: it is the system of record for its agents' working context, so its compression is a view, its cache is itself, and its retrieval is a GET on a doc id + rev with infinite TTL. This crown paper binds the five-lane deep investigation into one program: what the external evidence forbids, what our own fleet census actually costs, the retrieval and presentation halves of the doctrine, the security seam that must fail closed, and the two-level task board as the fully worked flagship. It ends with a go recommendation, a wave plan, and the judgment calls only the user can make.

blocks.text: 1 · Native-only is confirmed by every evidence class at once

content.value: (a) Supply chain: transitive dep ast-grep-cli 0.44.1 TROJANED; fresh installs still resolve the trojaned build today (#2462, #2267). (b) Economics: 2–7× measured cost increase, tokens_saved 0.00% across seven matched Claude Code runs (#2438). (c) Reliability: 502 retries burned a 5-hour org quota from 2% to 97% in 15 minutes; the proxy remained active after unwrap (#2340). (d) Protocol: signed thinking blocks corrupted → 400 (#2251); injected system message → 400 (#765). (e) Silent no-ops are the largest invisible-failure class in the tracker (18 open issues). The interview's native-only stance survives contact with everything. The audit-mode wrap survives only as a disposable caged instrument with a file-diff removal proof — or the user closes it on this evidence alone.

blocks.text: 2 · Nobody has ever measured a net win on the rail Barkpark pays for

content.value: Marketing says 60–95%. The vendor's own fleet median is 4.8%. The only independent study (tokbench, n=3, pre-registered, ledger-exact) measured real 5–8% per-request compression netting to

— Headroom had the lowest tokens-per-turn but the MOST turns (199 vs 163), and the turn-inflation cause is unresolved. And tokbench ran request-metered: nobody, vendor or independent, has measured Headroom on a cache-priced Anthropic rail. The honest prior for any compression layer is single-digit percent net — which is why the native path, which pays regardless, outranks every proxy path.
The bill is tokens-per-turn times turns — and nobody knows why the turns grew.

blocks.text: 3 · The failure taxonomy becomes five charter laws

content.value: Headroom's issue tracker is a complete failure taxonomy of guess-based compression over an ephemeral store. The store-fragility half (TTL cliffs #714, restart wipes #1809, permanently-empty stores #1023, hash-format drift #816/#1095, retry storms #1776, self-compress loops #1077) is structurally deleted by the handle doctrine — the architecture is the law. The presentation half must be adopted explicitly, each law priced by measured failure frequency and shipped with a per-emitter acceptance criterion:

Totals and truncation markers ride IN the payload, never in side-band metadata an adapter can drop
#2421: a truncated prefix re-presented as a complete 114-definition outline, 26 silently missing

A miss is a terminal, actionable error ('gone — re-run the source'), never a retryable 404

content.value: The doctrine (
ctx-compression-handle-doctrine

carried with an executable escape-hatch command; the store is the CMS; TTL is infinite; resolution is

blocks.text: bp park — foreign bulk becomes first-class documents

content.value: Anything an agent wants OUT of context — build logs, API responses, file dumps — parks as a document of a new park type in a
(isolation verdict confirmed across search, CLI, SSE, edges, and Studio: no cross-dataset search exists, so parked bulk can never pollute results). Addressing is content-addressed:

— the same bulk parked twice returns the existing handle with a dedup flag, so retry storms write once, and Headroom's entire hash-format-drift class cannot exist because one server produces and resolves one id scheme. The receipt is a handle plus a mandatory honest caller-supplied summary. A 2 MB body ceiling refuses loudly (naming media as the manual path — never auto-route: media today has no GC, no dedup, no size cap). GC ships as loud two-stage plumbing, schedule off by default. Park is deliberately NOT whale-crushing and NOT the Read class — the harness owns those; park's regime is the foreign-tool bulk where deterministic first/last-anchor elision is legitimate because guessing is all anyone has.

blocks.text: The four-piece kit — what every other surface inherits

items.value: Tier — a manifest-declared view per surface: the list card carries what the surface PAINTS (states, counts, flags), never what it might read. Fieldful nouns get projection views; blobful nouns get windows/handles.
Handle — doc_id + rev on every card, no exceptions. The handle IS the address, the cache key, and the CAS token. Bare rev always means document-CAS 32-hex.
Cache — content-addressed by rev, TTL infinite. The store is the CMS; there is no second store to wipe, drift, or expire.
Invalidation — a keyset feed of addresses, classed by event kind. Never TTL, never wall-clock, never 'once at session start'.
Honesty — staleness is badged, never silent; emptiness is tri-state (loading / synced-empty / stale); degraded paths are authored, not accidental.

blocks.text: Contradictions and resolutions — where the lanes collided

content.value: Five lanes wrote independently against the same repo; the collisions are few, and most resolve cleanly. Recorded openly, ruling by ruling.

blocks.text: Ruling 1 · rev rides every card — brief v3 AND a board profile

content.value: The one three-lane collision. All three architecture lanes agree rev joins the frozen brief card (brief v3): the handle anchor is missing from exactly the surfaces the doctrine needs it on (live-confirmed: today's ready card is 9 keys, none rev; search brief drops a _rev it already computed; the TUI decodes full view and throws rev away). The field census independently supports carriage: rev is already working agent vocabulary (7,920 command refs). Byte arithmetic: ~41 B/card keeps the realistic 50-card page 15% under its frozen tripwire; the hostile page squeaks by 76 B — accept the squeak or bump the ceiling with a recorded why (left to the user). The @brief_keys exact-set test and both byte tripwires are rewritten in the SAME PR, per the AXI amendment discipline.
Where the lanes genuinely disagreed:
ctx-compression-view-tiers-seam
recommended keeping views.supported frozen at [brief, full], while
ctx-compression-taskboard-flagship
needs a third
board

profile. The crown rules FOR the board profile. The flagship's consumer census is decisive: the board paints eight things brief v2 cut (rev, kind, labels, inserted_at, both dependency counts, per-rung criteria STATES, completeness inputs) and two brief-v2 cuts actively fight the merge machinery (seconds-truncated timestamps and claim-dropped-when-empty can strand a stale claimed row). Fattening brief instead would destroy the agent diet that is already paying measured dividends, and agents don't want per-rung states. The presentation lane's fear — unfreezing the 3-key manifest shape — becomes the acceptance criterion, not a veto: the board profile ships under charter law 7's opt-in emission dance, so stale strict-decode binaries never brick. content.value: The doctrine (

Context-compression program · CROWN PAPER · deep investigation capstone · 2026-07-23

Compress Presentation, Never Truth — the Barkpark Context-Compression Program

Headroom is a 61,459-star proxy that guesses what to compress — and its own 3,900-line self-audit concludes the guessing was the bug. Barkpark does not need to guess: it is the system of record for its agents' working context, so its compression is a view, its cache is itself, and its retrieval is a GET on a doc id + rev with infinite TTL. This crown paper binds the five-lane deep investigation into one program: what the external evidence forbids, what our own fleet census actually costs, the retrieval and presentation halves of the doctrine, the security seam that must fail closed, and the two-level task board as the fully worked flagship. It ends with a go recommendation, a wave plan, and the judgment calls only the user can make.

The crown of 5 lane papers · deep investigation · read-only run (papers only, no code) · Lanes: headroom-lessons · spend-census · handle-doctrine · view-tiers-seam · taskboard-flagship · Epic seed: filed as a considering-state task (task-funnel doctrine: considering precedes open)

The governing principle
Defer bulk, never meaning; compress presentation, never truth. Headroom compresses because it doesn't know the content. Barkpark doesn't need to guess — it is the system of record, so its compression is a view, its cache is itself, and its retrieval is a GET. Every ruling in this paper is an application of that sentence.

The grand view — from a 61k-star runtime to a one-sentence doctrine

The wish began as: study github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom and figure out how Barkpark can use it — aligned with Barkpark philosophy, avoiding the cons, plus the research that keeps us from doing anything stupid. The investigation's answer is an inversion: Headroom is not a runtime to adopt but a syllabus to strip-mine. Its flagship proxy ships with a 14-file REALIGNMENT self-audit in which ten parallel audit agents found five P0 cache-killer bugs affecting every customer and retired roughly 25,000 lines of code. The corrected mental model they converged on — passthrough is sacred, hash-keyed retrieval, position-preserving, deterministic — is a proxy painfully rediscovering what a system of record has by construction (ctx-compression-headroom-lessons).

The punchline: a CMS that renders brief views at the source has no proxy seam to violate. Tool output that is born brief cannot corrupt a stream it never rewrites, cannot bust a provider cache it never sits in front of, and cannot lose data behind a marker whose store it IS. Where Headroom must guess (SmartCrusher keep-set heuristics, hash stores with TTL cliffs, retrieval round limits), Barkpark declares: the brief card is a server render, the handle is a doc id + rev, and resolution is bp doc get.

Crucially, this is a second wave, not greenfield. The AXI brief-views epic already landed wave 1: ?view=brief on task.ready / task.prime / search.query, a manifest-declared views contract under the ?views=1 opt-in, a 48 KB rune-safe MCP clamp, and measured 12–92× diets. The program prepared here is the successor: generalize the tier pattern to every noun, add the retrieval half (handles, bp park, MCP resources), prove the wins with censuses and duels, seal the new read paths, and demonstrate the whole doctrine end-to-end in the task board. The diet already shows up in real transcripts: bp's share of fleet tool-result bytes fell from a pre-AXI 9.4% to 5.37% (ctx-compression-spend-census).

The paper map — five lanes, one crown

This paper stands alone; each lane paper holds one lane's full depth. Descend by slug when you want the evidence trail, the complete tables, or the coverage appendix that says what was checked and NOT found.

Lane paperOwnsIts decisive export
ctx-compression-headroom-lessonsAll external evidence: Headroom source, 256 open issues censused one by one, the REALIGNMENT audit, the only independent benchmarkThe verdict table (ADOPT/REJECT/TEST FIRST per mechanism), the five presentation laws, the audit-wrap cage spec, the savings calibration
ctx-compression-spend-censusAll internal evidence: fleet spend census (21,178 transcripts), field-usage census, harness overlap, meter calibration, experiment designsThe measured wave ranking; the two pilot reversals; the naming tax; the serialization duel result that met the interview's SmartCrusher pre-condition
ctx-compression-handle-doctrineThe retrieval half: handle grammar, rev vocabulary, bp park, ETag port, MCP resources + resource_link rulingSix laws L1–L6 + six buildable slices; the rev-carriage census across 11 surfaces; ~70% of the machinery already exists
ctx-compression-view-tiers-seamThe presentation half: the three-layer tier grammar, the fieldful/blobful boundary, the envelope/tenancy security reviewThe binding law (every view is a projection of the SEALED envelope) with a six-pattern proof obligation; three security findings
ctx-compression-taskboard-flagshipThe flagship worked example: two-level task board — board tier, focused tier, cache-by-rev, live invalidation, failure honestyThe four-piece kit every surface inherits; the board card frozen field by field; 22.5–27× measured; the un-truncation finding

What the external evidence forbids — Headroom, strip-mined

The full treatment is ctx-compression-headroom-lessons: every mechanism read at algorithm level, all 256 open non-PR issues classified, 25 horror issues read in full. Three findings carry the epic.

1 · Native-only is confirmed by every evidence class at once

No Headroom runtime near keys or prod — ever
(a) Supply chain: transitive dep ast-grep-cli 0.44.1 TROJANED; fresh installs still resolve the trojaned build today (#2462, #2267). (b) Economics: 2–7× measured cost increase, tokens_saved 0.00% across seven matched Claude Code runs (#2438). (c) Reliability: 502 retries burned a 5-hour org quota from 2% to 97% in 15 minutes; the proxy remained active after unwrap (#2340). (d) Protocol: signed thinking blocks corrupted → 400 (#2251); injected system message → 400 (#765). (e) Silent no-ops are the largest invisible-failure class in the tracker (18 open issues). The interview's native-only stance survives contact with everything. The audit-mode wrap survives only as a disposable caged instrument with a file-diff removal proof — or the user closes it on this evidence alone.

2 · Nobody has ever measured a net win on the rail Barkpark pays for

Marketing says 60–95%. The vendor's own fleet median is 4.8%. The only independent study (tokbench, n=3, pre-registered, ledger-exact) measured real 5–8% per-request compression netting to +17.8% median billed cost — Headroom had the lowest tokens-per-turn but the MOST turns (199 vs 163), and the turn-inflation cause is unresolved. And tokbench ran request-metered: nobody, vendor or independent, has measured Headroom on a cache-priced Anthropic rail. The honest prior for any compression layer is single-digit percent net — which is why the native path, which pays regardless, outranks every proxy path.

The bill is tokens-per-turn times turns — and nobody knows why the turns grew.

3 · The failure taxonomy becomes five charter laws

Headroom's issue tracker is a complete failure taxonomy of guess-based compression over an ephemeral store. The store-fragility half (TTL cliffs #714, restart wipes #1809, permanently-empty stores #1023, hash-format drift #816/#1095, retry storms #1776, self-compress loops #1077) is structurally deleted by the handle doctrine — the architecture is the law. The presentation half must be adopted explicitly, each law priced by measured failure frequency and shipped with a per-emitter acceptance criterion:

LawStatementThe issue that proves it
L1 · Completeness in-payloadTotals and truncation markers ride IN the payload, never in side-band metadata an adapter can drop#2421: a truncated prefix re-presented as a complete 114-definition outline, 26 silently missing
L2 · Dead handles fail terminallyA miss is a terminal, actionable error ('gone — re-run the source'), never a retryable 404#1776: one agent retried a dead hash 25× in 11 minutes; 6% store-miss rate
L3 · Deterministic, stably-ordered outputrender(doc, rev) is byte-identical every call; volatile values never ride agent views#294: one dynamic tools array busted the entire provider prefix cache; cache writes are 58.4% of our fleet cost
L4 · Always keep errorsA brief view may drop bulk, never failure signalsthe silent no-op class — 18 open issues of 'Optimization Enabled' while nothing worked
L5 · Observation-only feedbackCensuses between releases, never per-request adaptation; no numeric threshold without a census behind itHeadroom's 50%/80% retrieval thresholds are bare constants with no derivation anywhere — folklore

Good news, measured: bp is already nearly L3-compliant. bp capabilities and bp task ready are byte-identical across consecutive live calls; the vendored MCP go-sdk sorts tools by name and resources by URI on every list (mcp/features.go:103, server.go:191-193); no clock or randomness touches bp's emitted payloads. The entire residue is two volatile search fields (ms, searchEventId) and a tripwire lint to keep it true.

Where the tokens actually go — the fleet's own price list

The internal evidence lane (ctx-compression-spend-census) ran a stdlib-only census over the whole transcript corpus — 44 project directories, 21,178 JSONL files, 2.05 GB of tool-result bytes — and it corrected the easy story twice before settling the ranking.

What enters contextBytesShare

Reversal one: the 12-session pilot said input bulk beats results; fleet-wide it inverts — results 71.8% vs 26.4% input-side (64.3% vs 33.5% even excluding the one 609 MB Read-outlier project). Output-side work ranks first. Reversal two: big results are NOT rare — ≥10 KB results hold 68.1% of result bytes — but the whales are Read file content the harness's own primitives (subagent isolation, overflow-to-file) already own, not bp payloads. So Headroom-style whale-crushing stays the wrong frame: bp's honest park target is the foreign-tool class (gh, git, curl, python output — roughly 28% of fleet result bytes), and bp itself is a single-digit share (5.37%).

Under these economics the cost driver is turns, not payload spikes — tokbench proved what happens when you ignore that. Two consequences shape everything downstream: (1) the un-briefed capabilities manifest (95,666 B, consumed at session start where bytes are ~5–6× amplified) is the single biggest prize; (2) a brief card missing one needed field forces a follow-up task get that usually costs more than the cut saved — agents already handle-climb (12,368 task get calls vs 1,421 task ready). Brief-but-COMPLETE beats smaller-but-lossy.

The naming tax — the cheapest win in the whole program
Agents typed the nonexistent bp task show 2,428 times and bp task list 329 times in one project corpus — over 1.1 MB of guaranteed-useless error responses plus a wasted turn each. An alias or did-you-mean hint is cheaper than any view-tier work and pays on every future session.

The serialization result — the interview's pre-condition is met

The interview ruled that porting Headroom's SmartCrusher to Go is not a committed path: a deterministic tabular render profile should be tested against our own data first. It was, and it wins — reviving AXI's explicitly deferred R6:

PayloadCompact JSONTSV renderByte win

Lossless, deterministic, prefix-stable by construction — no Python, no ML, no information loss. Headroom's own evolution predicted this: it added a lossless-first csv-schema stage and gave it a LOWER savings bar (15%) than the lossy path, explicitly because lossless output needs no retrieval round-trip. Statistical crushing is unnecessary on declared-schema data. One hard caveat rides every number: these are BYTES. No count_tokens-capable API key was reachable from the run environment, and the meter standard bans tiktoken and chars/4 substitutes — the fixtures sit ready, and 12 count_tokens calls are epic task #1.

The retrieval half — a handle is a claim you can always cash

The doctrine (ctx-compression-handle-doctrine) is one sentence: a handle is the JSON triple {doc_id, type, rev} carried with an executable escape-hatch command; the store is the CMS; TTL is infinite; resolution is bp doc get. rev is the existing opaque 32-hex CAS token — equality-only staleness (fresh or moved-on, never 'n revisions behind'). Barkpark is roughly 70% prebuilt for this: _rev rides every envelope read (projection-protected — ?fields= cannot strip it), rev + previousRev ride the mutation ledger, both SSE legs, and the task events feed; CAS fencing runs through one chokepoint (mutations.ex:726); and the CAS seam's two known holes were fixed and merged before this run (PR #2381, #5720) — the doctrine stands on an audited seam.

LawRulingAnchor / evidence
L1 · GrammarHandle = {doc_id, type, rev} + executable escape hatch (AXI help[] style). NOT a universal URI — barkpark:// stays MCP-resource-space only; tenancy binds resolutionthe {"_ref": id} grammar already accepts bare ids (expand.ex:247) — extend, don't invent
L2 · Equality-only stalenessrev is unordered by construction (16 random bytes hex per write)writer.ex generate_rev
L3 · Latest-with-rev-honestyResolution returns current truth + _rev; mismatch = loud staleness signal. True rev-PINNED retrieval explicitly deferredRevision rows never store the rev string (revision.ex) — pinning is unbuildable without a schema change, and no consumer needs it
L4 · One rev vocabularyBare rev always means document CAS 32-hex; Papers' monotonic int is always qualified (--if-rev / paper_rev), never barethe split is clean today purely by accident — no written rule exists
L5 · Never rewrap, never soft-missHandle-resolution output is never re-briefed; a miss is terminal and actionableHeadroom #1077 (self-compress infinite loop), #1776 (25-retry storm)
L6 · No silent expiryInfinite TTL ≠ no GC: park GC is loud, two-stage (flag → grace → delete), every stage eventedPlaygroundReaper is the in-house model; Headroom #714/#1809 are the counter-model

bp park — foreign bulk becomes first-class documents

Anything an agent wants OUT of context — build logs, API responses, file dumps — parks as a document of a new park type in a dedicated per-project park dataset (isolation verdict confirmed across search, CLI, SSE, edges, and Studio: no cross-dataset search exists, so parked bulk can never pollute results). Addressing is content-addressed: park-<sha256[:12]> — the same bulk parked twice returns the existing handle with a dedup flag, so retry storms write once, and Headroom's entire hash-format-drift class cannot exist because one server produces and resolves one id scheme. The receipt is a handle plus a mandatory honest caller-supplied summary. A 2 MB body ceiling refuses loudly (naming media as the manual path — never auto-route: media today has no GC, no dedup, no size cap). GC ships as loud two-stage plumbing, schedule off by default. Park is deliberately NOT whale-crushing and NOT the Read class — the harness owns those; park's regime is the foreign-tool bulk where deterministic first/last-anchor elision is legitimate because guessing is all anyone has.

MCP — the URI space grows; resource_link demoted to opt-in

The pre-storm plan (dual-carry brief text + resource_link 'because clients that ignore links lose nothing') was overturned by evidence: wild clients don't ignore unknown content items — Kiro and Cline hard-crash the whole tool call (Kiro#9104, cline#5208). Ruling: the text handle (JSON + command template) is the canonical carrier on every surface; barkpark://tasks/{id} and barkpark://park/{id} resources ship now (the papers-as-resources template pattern already exists in mcp_resources.go); resource_link items ship behind an opt-in flag until a live four-client smoke test passes. The pinned go-sdk v1.6.1 already carries ResourceLink, so flipping the flag later costs nothing. And the whole MCP wave sequences AFTER deliberate exercise sessions: the entire transcript corpus contains exactly 4 barkpark MCP calls, ever — passive history cannot rank this surface.

ETag — a port, not an invention

Corrected premise: /v1/data doc reads ALREADY have ETag/304 (QueryController: doc_etag IS the rev; list_etag hashes id:rev pairs). What's missing is the Tasks controller — /v1/tasks, /prime, /events have zero conditional GET. The port must fix two flaws the precedent itself has: fold the view param into the etag (two view shapes of the same docs must never share one — a latent RFC 9110 violation today) and emit Vary — absent everywhere in the API. The client half exists (GetConditional proven); the taskboard currently hardcodes an empty If-None-Match and throws the server's ETag away. One honesty note travels with the port: the ETag is computed after the full query+render, so a 304 saves wire, not server work — name it, so nobody calls it a cache win it isn't.

The presentation half — one tier grammar, and a seam that fails closed

The presentation lane (ctx-compression-view-tiers-seam) refuses the naive move (merge the three tier mechanisms that already coexist) and ratifies a three-layer grammar instead — because the brief card's 20–80× wins came from nine hand-measured cuts a generic field list cannot express.

LayerMechanismWho declares itStatus
1 · Named views?view=brief|full — the manifest/transport contract per command; CLI and MCP inherit generically (run.go resolveView is fully manifest-driven — new nouns need ZERO Go changes)the manifest, via the shared agent_views_descriptor()shipped on task.ready / task.prime / search.query
2 · Field projection?fields= — the caller-driven escape valve, always applied post-sealthe caller, per requestshipped on /v1/data/query, /v1/data/doc, search

Fieldful nouns get views; blobful nouns get handles.

The two-regime boundary is sharp in the live census: a paper compresses 442× via fields=title (153 KB/doc → 346 B — the whole weight is one blob) while a task compresses 17× — field-dropping cannot compress a blob. Blobful nouns (papers, sheets) get windowing and (doc_id, rev) handles; fieldful nouns (tasks, tickets, tags, media docs) get declared brief views. And hand-tuning stays worth ~20% on top of generic projection: 271 B/card hand-tuned vs 335 B/doc generic — Layer 3 is the default, never a straitjacket.

The binding law and the proof obligation

Per-slice proof obligation (proposed charter law)
Every epic slice that adds a view, a handle, or any new emitter ships the applicable protective patterns in the same PR, each proven able to fail: redact-then-assert-omitted, cross-tenant-then-404 (no count oracle), opt-out-byte-identical, byte-ceiling tripwire pair (realistic + hostile), ETag cache-key completeness, exact-key-set pin. All six patterns have live precedents to copy (catalogued at file:line in the lane paper). A green that the right thing did not produce counts for nothing.

The security review — three findings

FindingVerdictRecommendation
field_readable? nil-polarity inversion — nil means UNRESTRICTED (envelope.ex:222) while render/3 treats nil as most-restrictive: opposite polarities on sibling functionsReal but DEAD: the census classified every caller — zero HTTP-reachable nil call sitesFlip nil to fail-closed AND fence it with a CI grep — the census proves the flip breaks nothing, the fence stops the next hand-rolled emitter from regrowing the hazard
The unsealed task-embed chain: tasks/query.ex to_render_map reads doc.content directly (zero Envelope references) and feeds TaskResolver → paper reader task-embeds + Studio preview. Same file proves the double standard: board.ex gates every field; query.ex, wired into papers.ex, does notLatent today (no private task field exists) — but the epic builds its flagship directly on this mechanismSeal NOW, copying board.ex's field_readable? gate verbatim, before any tier stacks on it — with the redact-then-assert proof attached
Export-class emitters (cycle_fleet_controller release paths, onixedit/sheets exports, bulldocs_form, media_processing) emit raw content with zero Envelope references — intentional, but none would inherit a future per-field privacy ruleUnlegislated classOne slice writes the export-class law: every full-content emitter either routes through Envelope or carries a recorded, tested exemption. No third state

Handle resolution inherits three laws from this seam: visibility is evaluated at READ time under the CURRENT schema (the revision-redaction precedent, history_controller.ex:19-38); the route lives INSIDE the scoped pipelines (a handle endpoint mounted outside ResolveWorkspace silently goes global — pin the pipeline, prove with a cross-workspace-404 test); and projection never widens rows (perspective resolves before retrieval; views touch only post-retrieval shaping).

The flagship — the two-level task board, worked end to end

The flagship lane (ctx-compression-taskboard-flagship) proves the doctrine composes. Every hard part of a two-level split already exists in the Go TUI — snapshot cache, live SSE spine, forward-only merge, honest connection states, rev-CAS writes, and a replay-safe events feed with ZERO consumers. Only the wire is monolithic: every paint pulls 9.14 MB of full-depth JSON to draw rows that need 0.4 MB, and a quiet open board burns ~1.2 GB/hour of decoded JSON. Studio's LiveView board already improvised the pattern (compact server-projected cards + a fresh per-doc peek read) — the epic formalizes what Studio proved live.

The design: a board tier on a manifest-declared board view (22.5–27× lighter, measured live); a focused tier on the views-free task.get (14 KB), fetched on focus with cursor±2 / NOW-band / NEXT-strip prefetch, reqID fencing, and pause-on-mutation (the superfile and lazygit patterns); cache-by-rev — details content-addressed by (doc_id, rev), TTL infinite, sound because mutation_events is append-only and gap-free with no horizon; live invalidation classed by event KIND from /v1/tasks/events; and failure honesty throughout — staleness badged never silent, tri-state emptiness, authored degradation paths.

Events never carry truth — they carry addresses.

The iron rule survives amended: board-tier refetch stays WHOLE (at 85 KB gzip it is cheap and provably drift-free — and one write class, bare dependency-edge adds on non-in_progress tasks, is invisible to the feed, which whole-refetch covers and a per-event patcher would not). Per-address granularity applies only to the detail cache, where the address (doc_id + rev) is exactly what an event carries. The event-kind classes are load-bearing because task.pulse bumps rev on EVERY lease renewal while touching nothing the board paints — naive rev-diff invalidation would thrash every active card; kind-classed invalidation keeps-and-badges instead. And task.criterion proves the classes don't align with board-vs-detail field boundaries: it lives in a detail key but moves the board's met/total.

The design renegotiates frozen contracts — say so, never slip it
Charter decisions D12 ('preview NEVER fetches') and D13/D28 ('zero extra fetches — the wire already carries everything') are frozen contracts that celebrate exactly what this design dismantles. The epic charter must open with explicit unfreezing language and the evidence that earned it (9.14 MB per paint, 32% corpus truncation). The four-piece kit — what every other surface inherits

  • Cache — content-addressed by rev, TTL infinite. The store is the CMS; there is no second store to wipe, drift, or expire.
  • Invalidation — a keyset feed of addresses, classed by event kind. Never TTL, never wall-clock, never 'once at session start'.
  • Honesty — staleness is badged, never silent; emptiness is tri-state (loading / synced-empty / stale); degraded paths are authored, not accidental.

Compress Presentation, Never Truth — the Barkpark Context-Compression Program

Headroom is a 61,459-star proxy that guesses what to compress — and its own 3,900-line self-audit concludes the guessing was the bug. Barkpark does not need to guess: it is the system of record for its agents' working context, so its compression is a view, its cache is itself, and its retrieval is a GET on a doc id + rev with infinite TTL. This crown paper binds the five-lane deep investigation into one program: what the external evidence forbids, what our own fleet census actually costs, the retrieval and presentation halves of the doctrine, the security seam that must fail closed, and the two-level task board as the fully worked flagship. It ends with a go recommendation, a wave plan, and the judgment calls only the user can make.

The governing principle Defer bulk, never meaning; compress presentation, never truth. Headroom compresses because it doesn't know the content. Barkpark doesn't need to guess — it is the system of record, so its compression is a view, its cache is itself, and its retrieval is a GET. Every ruling in this paper is an application of that sentence.

The grand view — from a 61k-star runtime to a one-sentence doctrine

The wish began as: study github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom and figure out how Barkpark can use it — aligned with Barkpark philosophy, avoiding the cons, plus the research that keeps us from doing anything stupid. The investigation's answer is an inversion: Headroom is not a runtime to adopt but a syllabus to strip-mine. Its flagship proxy ships with a 14-file REALIGNMENT self-audit in which ten parallel audit agents found five P0 cache-killer bugs affecting every customer and retired roughly 25,000 lines of code. The corrected mental model they converged on — passthrough is sacred, hash-keyed retrieval, position-preserving, deterministic — is a proxy painfully rediscovering what a system of record has by construction (ctx-compression-headroom-lessons).

The punchline: a CMS that renders brief views at the source has no proxy seam to violate. Tool output that is born brief cannot corrupt a stream it never rewrites, cannot bust a provider cache it never sits in front of, and cannot lose data behind a marker whose store it IS. Where Headroom must guess (SmartCrusher keep-set heuristics, hash stores with TTL cliffs, retrieval round limits), Barkpark declares: the brief card is a server render, the handle is a doc id + rev, and resolution is bp doc get.

Crucially, this is a second wave, not greenfield. The AXI brief-views epic already landed wave 1: ?view=brief on task.ready / task.prime / search.query, a manifest-declared views contract under the ?views=1 opt-in, a 48 KB rune-safe MCP clamp, and measured 12–92× diets. The program prepared here is the successor: generalize the tier pattern to every noun, add the retrieval half (handles, bp park, MCP resources), prove the wins with censuses and duels, seal the new read paths, and demonstrate the whole doctrine end-to-end in the task board. The diet already shows up in real transcripts: bp's share of fleet tool-result bytes fell from a pre-AXI 9.4% to 5.37% (ctx-compression-spend-census).

The paper map — five lanes, one crown

This paper stands alone; each lane paper holds one lane's full depth. Descend by slug when you want the evidence trail, the complete tables, or the coverage appendix that says what was checked and NOT found.

What the external evidence forbids — Headroom, strip-mined

The full treatment is ctx-compression-headroom-lessons: every mechanism read at algorithm level, all 256 open non-PR issues classified, 25 horror issues read in full. Three findings carry the epic.

1 · Native-only is confirmed by every evidence class at once

No Headroom runtime near keys or prod — ever (a) Supply chain: transitive dep ast-grep-cli 0.44.1 TROJANED; fresh installs still resolve the trojaned build today (#2462, #2267). (b) Economics: 2–7× measured cost increase, tokens_saved 0.00% across seven matched Claude Code runs (#2438). (c) Reliability: 502 retries burned a 5-hour org quota from 2% to 97% in 15 minutes; the proxy remained active after unwrap (#2340). (d) Protocol: signed thinking blocks corrupted → 400 (#2251); injected system message → 400 (#765). (e) Silent no-ops are the largest invisible-failure class in the tracker (18 open issues). The interview's native-only stance survives contact with everything. The audit-mode wrap survives only as a disposable caged instrument with a file-diff removal proof — or the user closes it on this evidence alone.

2 · Nobody has ever measured a net win on the rail Barkpark pays for

Marketing says 60–95%. The vendor's own fleet median is 4.8%. The only independent study (tokbench, n=3, pre-registered, ledger-exact) measured real 5–8% per-request compression netting to +17.8% median billed cost — Headroom had the lowest tokens-per-turn but the MOST turns (199 vs 163), and the turn-inflation cause is unresolved. And tokbench ran request-metered: nobody, vendor or independent, has measured Headroom on a cache-priced Anthropic rail. The honest prior for any compression layer is single-digit percent net — which is why the native path, which pays regardless, outranks every proxy path.

The bill is tokens-per-turn times turns — and nobody knows why the turns grew.

3 · The failure taxonomy becomes five charter laws

Headroom's issue tracker is a complete failure taxonomy of guess-based compression over an ephemeral store. The store-fragility half (TTL cliffs #714, restart wipes #1809, permanently-empty stores #1023, hash-format drift #816/#1095, retry storms #1776, self-compress loops #1077) is structurally deleted by the handle doctrine — the architecture is the law. The presentation half must be adopted explicitly, each law priced by measured failure frequency and shipped with a per-emitter acceptance criterion:

Good news, measured: bp is already nearly L3-compliant. bp capabilities and bp task ready are byte-identical across consecutive live calls; the vendored MCP go-sdk sorts tools by name and resources by URI on every list (mcp/features.go:103, server.go:191-193); no clock or randomness touches bp's emitted payloads. The entire residue is two volatile search fields (ms, searchEventId) and a tripwire lint to keep it true.

Where the tokens actually go — the fleet's own price list

The internal evidence lane (ctx-compression-spend-census) ran a stdlib-only census over the whole transcript corpus — 44 project directories, 21,178 JSONL files, 2.05 GB of tool-result bytes — and it corrected the easy story twice before settling the ranking.

Reversal one: the 12-session pilot said input bulk beats results; fleet-wide it inverts — results 71.8% vs 26.4% input-side (64.3% vs 33.5% even excluding the one 609 MB Read-outlier project). Output-side work ranks first. Risks, unknowns, and the recommendation

The top risk: fighting the last war Headroom's failures are a proxy's failures. The trap is deriving smugness instead of laws — Barkpark can still violate every law natively: a brief view that hides errors (L4), a census that feeds back per-request (L5), a payload that busts caches (L3), a declared brief that is mediocre without per-noun tuning, a cache layer that goes silently stale. Being the system of record removes the seam, not the responsibility. That is why every law ships with a per-emitter acceptance criterion and every slice carries the fail-closed proof obligation.
  • Declared briefs may underperform hand-tuning (the 20–80× wins were hand-measured). Mitigated: caps ride the declaration, tripwires are mandatory, hand-tuned serializers stay legal.
  • Reopening frozen contracts (brief card, D12/D13/D28, views.supported) is deliberate and must be explicit — the amendment discipline exists; drift risk is nonzero.
